thread.title: S&P 500, Dow Jones Futures Fall As Trump Taps John Bolton, China Retaliates; These 2 Hot Techs Crush Views

author: ED CARSON
title: S&P 500, Dow Jones Futures Fall As Trump Taps John Bolton, China Retaliates; These 2 Hot Techs Crush Views
text:
Futures for the S&P 500 index, Dow Jones industrial average and Nasdaq 100 fell Friday morning after President Donald Trump said late Thursday that John Bolton will replace H.R. McMaster as his national security advisor and China laid out its retaliatory measures against U.S. imports. The stock market's major averages plunged more than 2% Thursday on Trump's decision to impose tariffs on $60 billion in Chinese imports, saying it was "the first of many" actions.
X Meanwhile Micron Technology ( MU ) and Smart Global Holdings ( SGH ), two top stocks from the No. 1-rated data storage group, easily beat earnings views and raised guidance in late trading. Nike rallied on strong results as it sees a U.S. revival.
Meanwhile, Trump continued to make headlines late. Trump tweeted late that Bolton, former U.S. ambassador to the U.N., will replace McMaster in April.
I am pleased to announce that, effective 4/9/18, @AmbJohnBolton will be my new National Security Advisor. I am very thankful for the service of General H.R. McMaster who has done an outstanding job & will always remain my friend. There will be an official contact handover on 4/9.
— Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) March 22, 2018 

Trump recently tapped to CIA Director Mike Pompeo to replace Rex Tillerson as secretary of state. Both Bolton and Pompeo are hardliners on Iran and opponents of that regime's nuclear deal with the U.S. and other world powers.

Please contact customer service CLOSE China announced late Thursday that it was raising tariffs on some 128 U.S. products worth $3 billion, including pork, aluminum and other goods. But China could do far more, curbing Boeing ( BA ) jet purchases, reducing soyabean imports and setting an export duty on Apple ( AAPL ) iPhones and other tech gear.
During Thursday's stock market trading , the Nasdaq composite tumbled 2.4%, joining the S&P 500 index and Dow Jones below the 50-day moving average. The S&P 500 lost 2.5% and the Dow Jones 2.9%, with Boeing losing 5.2%.
One positive note: The put/call ratio hit a level typically associated with short-term bottoms, providing some hope that the stock market can get at least a temporary boost .
S&P 500 futures fell 0.3% vs. fair value, but that was well off overnight lows. Nasdaq 100 futures lost 0.8%. Dow Jones futures slid 0.3%, even with Nike's 5% early Friday boost.
